subject: Operator/Controller split and SCCs — DPA redline follow-up
messages:
From: Clara Hansen <clara.hansen@edgecloud.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Operator/Controller split and SCCs — DPA redline follow-up

Ben — thanks again for the call this morning. A few follow-ups from EdgeCloud Legal: we need clearer language in the MSA/Order Form about the operator vs controller split for our joint features (logging, monitoring, customer-supplied prompts). Specifically:

- Can you confirm which party is the controller for telemetry/usage data vs model-derived outputs?
- We need a DPA redline that aligns with the EU SCCs (2021) and a short transfer-impact addendum for non-EEA subprocessors.
- Please include KMS options (customer-managed keys) and whether Dedicated or Private deployment options satisfy onshore-processing requirements.

Attached: we will share a PO stub and our standard procurement checklist once commercial terms are aligned. Can you route to your legal team and get a redline by EoW? Also cc procurement (procurements@edgecloud.com) after legal signoff so we can kick DocuSign.

Best,
Clara
Clara Hansen
Senior Counsel, EdgeCloud Systems

Subject: Re: Operator/Controller split and SCCs — DPA redline follow-up

Clara — thanks, understood. Looping in Laura (legal) and Jordan (account lead). Proposed next steps from my side:

1) Laura to propose specific redline language for the MSA/DPA and a short transfer-impact addendum.
2) We will confirm whether Dedicated (reserved capacity) + customer KMS meets your onshore requirement and produce a brief ops note for your team.
3) If EdgeCloud prefers a binding SCCs execution path, we can prepare an SCCs execution plan and estimate the time/cost.

Jordan — are there commercial constraints we should flag (pricing/lead times) if EdgeCloud asks for EU-only processing via Dedicated capacity?

I’ll hold off on procurement until legal is aligned.

Thanks —

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Clara Hansen <clara.hansen@edgecloud.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 13:45:00 +0100
Subject: RE: Operator/Controller split and SCCs — DPA redline follow-up

Clara — thanks for the clear ask. I reviewed the MSA and Order Form and drafted targeted redlines attached (redwood-dpa-redline-v1.docx). Key notes and proposed language below (high level):

- Roles: we recommend clarifying that EdgeCloud is Controller for customer-provided content and outputs intended for EdgeCloud
  and Redwood acts as Processor for telemetry, inference execution, and model-serving infrastructure, except where Redwood takes independent decisions about purposes (in which case we propose a limited Controller carveout and associated lawful basis).

- SCCs: include reference to the EU Commission standard contractual clauses (2021). We propose selecting the Controller-to-Processor module where applicable and appending an SCCs execution exhibit. See attached sccs-execution-plan.pdf for project plan (evidence, DPO contact, subprocessors list refresh cadence).

- Transfer-impact addendum: short paragraph to capture on-prem/DEDICATED-case fallback when subprocessor footprint extends outside EEA; includes commitments to supplementary safeguards (encryption at rest, KMS options, logging minimization).

Suggested contract snippets (for your counsel):
"Redwood shall process Personal Data only on documented instructions from EdgeCloud, acting as Processor. Where Redwood processes Personal Data for its own purposes and independent decision-making occurs, the parties shall document such processing and identify the lawful basis and data categories in Schedule X."

Timeline: we can produce a tracked redline + SCCs exhibit within 3 business days (internal review) and are prepared to negotiate a single narrow carveout if EdgeCloud needs limited Controller status for specific analytics flows. If we accept an EU-dedicated hosting requirement, there is a commercial uplift — Jordan, please provide a 90-day estimate for Dedicated capacity provisioning and delta pricing.

Attachments: redwood-dpa-redline-v1.docx; sccs-execution-plan.pdf

Happy to hop on a 30-min legal call if that helps.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Director, Legal — Contracts & Privacy
laura_bennett@redwood.com

From: Clara Hansen <clara.hansen@edgecloud.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: procurements@edgecloud.com
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 10:17:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Operator/Controller split and SCCs — DPA redline follow-up

Thanks Laura and Ben — this is exactly what we needed. A few quick clarifications from procurement and legal: 

- EdgeCloud can accept the Controller/Processor allocation proposed, provided the transfer-impact addendum includes a subprocessor notification window (10 business days) and a right to object to high-risk subprocessors.
- We will sign SCCs if Redwood confirms that the SCCs exhibit will be kept up to date and that subprocessor changes trigger the notification cadence in the sccs-execution-plan.pdf.
- Procurement attached a PO stub (EdgeCloud_PO_789.pdf) to start the purchasing flow; we will wait for final redline and DocuSign link.

Procurement note for Jordan: if Dedicated EU capacity is required, please include the expected provisioning lead time and delta on the order form. Otherwise we will accept the standard hosted path with SCCs plus the transfer-impact addendum.

Please send the DocuSign link once redlines are finalized.

Best —
Clara
Clara Hansen
Senior Counsel, EdgeCloud Systems
procurements@edgecloud.com
